basics.name: Stéphan Zych
basics.tagline: Lead Developer · Application & Web Architect · Technical Lead

summary: Hands-on lead developer and application architect, 15+ years across agency, founder and international consulting work. I design web and application architecture in the PHP and JavaScript/TypeScript ecosystems, own the technical decisions around it (stack choices, project structure, standards, code review), and keep implementing alongside the team.
I also focus on how software gets built and shipped: reusable project foundations, containerised environments, CI/CD, automated deployments and disciplined AI-assisted engineering.

experience.summary: Hands-on lead developer in the technical team that came out of the Cherry Pulp integration, currently four to five engineers. I develop day to day while leading technical direction and the modernisation of how the team builds and ships.

groups.label: Architecture & technical direction
items: Own architecture and technical decisions across concurrent projects: stack choices, project structure, and the boundaries between backend, API and frontend
Define technical standards, development conventions and code review practice, and drive their adoption across teams
Maintain and evolve the internal tooling and project boilerplates originally built at Cherry Pulp and still in use within CBTW
Support developers through review and technical guidance while remaining in the codebase
Work across distributed international teams, including enterprise environments using Microsoft internal tooling and AWS

groups.label: Platform & delivery modernisation (in progress)
items: Introduced a shared Docker local development environment (Traefik, PHP, MariaDB, phpMyAdmin) as the common baseline for projects
Building GitLab CI pipelines and secured containerised deployment on AWS Lightsail, replacing manual and FTP-based deployment and moving off Laravel Forge
Adding observability with Grafana, Prometheus and Loki
Rolled out project by project alongside ongoing client delivery: legacy workflows and the new pipeline currently run side by side

experience.period: 2013 – 2024 · acquired by CBTW in 2023, transition completed in 2024
experience.summary: Co-founded Cherry Pulp and helped grow it into a digital agency of around 20 people building custom websites, digital platforms and web applications. My role ran from frontend leadership into technical ownership across the company, hands-on throughout.

groups.label: Scale & impact
items: Delivered 200+ web platforms and digital products
Helped grow the company from 4 to 20 people
Supported and mentored development teams, up to 10–12 developers at peak

groups.label: Technical ownership & delivery
items: Designed a modular web delivery approach around Docker, WordPress with Bedrock, structured conventions and custom Forge/Lightsail deployment workflows, making setup faster and delivery more consistent across teams
Defined technical direction and project architecture across client work: stack selection, project structure, and the boundaries between WordPress or Laravel backends, APIs and JavaScript frontends
Owned frontend technical direction and the delivery of short-cycle web projects: WordPress from small to medium complexity, Laravel applications where the problem justified it
Established reusable boilerplates, conventions and CLI tooling that made project setup faster and maintenance predictable over time
Led technical scoping, estimation and client-facing technical advisory through discovery and delivery
Took part in technical hiring and onboarding, and set the standards new developers worked to

evidence.label: stephan.zych.be, two runtimes from one content source
evidence.detail: One Markdown/JSON content source feeds two independent runtimes: an Eleventy/Lit/TypeScript web application and a Go SSH/TUI application. GitHub Actions validates the repository, builds both container images separately, publishes them to GHCR and deploys automatically to DigitalOcean.

evidence.label: Developer tooling around coding agents
evidence.detail: A Go tool renders one canonical source (agents, skills, MCP servers, rules and reusable instructions) into the configuration of several coding-agent CLIs, so the same engineering rules apply whichever tool is driving; prompt.nvim carries those workflows into the editor. Agent work runs on deterministic checks, reviewed diffs and Git worktrees, with sandboxing (Bubblewrap, Landlock, seccomp) kept outside the agent's control.
